answer: A market seat opens only when a clerk watches one quill write a page on a mill-issued ivory sheet whose serial is registered to that key, and the page draws 2 grams of violet ink from a vial metered to the same key. Example: 4 fake keys need 4 sheets, 4 vials, and 4 witnessed hours, because one hand cannot finish two pages in the same hour. The seat fails if the sheet serial is reused or the dried ink mass misses the vial debit.
